I have farmed in Quzhou for a long time, so I do not start from zero. I start from what has held yield on my own land and what I see working on nearby fields. With 12 mu and only 2 people in the house, I will keep the plan steady and not spread myself too thin. I will put 8 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and 4 mu into cotton. Wheat-maize is still my backbone because I have well water, the land suits it, and cash comes back more steadily. Cotton I will keep on a smaller block, because it can still make money, but it asks for more spraying and more field watching. Since fertilizer is expensive but a bad harvest costs more, I will not cut rates too hard. I will feed wheat enough to push tillers and grain, maize enough to hold ear size, and cotton enough to keep bolls setting without letting the plants go too soft. On my land, I will use improved or hybrid seed, stay close to what has worked in recent years, irrigate on time instead of gambling on rain, and keep pesticide sprays to the number that matches the pressure I usually see. That is how I will manage risk, labor, and money together this year.
